title.en: Explain why it is the essence of management

say.en: Each musician in an orchestra may be brilliant, but without a conductor the music becomes noise. Coordination is the conductor of an organisation. In this lesson: Define coordination.
State its features.
Explain why it is the essence of management.

body.en: *Coordination* is the process by which a manager synchronises the activities of different departments so that the organisation acts as one. It integrates group efforts, ensures unity of action, is a continuous process, is all-pervasive, is the responsibility of all managers, and is a deliberate function: a manager must coordinate consciously even when people are willing to cooperate.

Coordination synchronises them so that the firm acts as one towards a common goal.
Why is it needed? Growth in size, functional differentiation and specialisation.
It is continuous, all-pervasive, every manager's job, and deliberate. So it is the essence of management.

explanation.en: Coordination is not a separate function but the force that binds all the functions together.

passage.en: Coordination integrates __1__ efforts and ensures unity of __2__. It is a __3__ process, is needed in every function and at every level, and is the responsibility of __4__ managers. It is a __5__ function: a manager must coordinate on purpose even when people are willing to cooperate. That is why it is called the __6__ of management.

say.en: Complete the paragraph about coordination.

body.en: As an organisation grows in size, the number of people and departments increases. Functional differentiation makes departments pursue their own goals, and specialisation makes specialists think they alone know best. *Coordination* ties all of these together. Since it is needed in every function and at every level, it is called the essence of management.

points.en: *Needed* at every level and in every function

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A fan company's production department made 60,000 fans last quarter, but the sales department could sell only 45,000. What does this show, and how many fans are left unsold?

say.en: Let us work this out together. A fan company's production department made 60,000 fans last quarter, but the sales department could sell only 45,000. What does this show, and how many fans are left unsold?
Unsold fans equals 60,000 minus 45,000 equals 15,000.
That is 15,000 divided by 60,000 times 100 equals 25 percent of output lying in stock.
Production and sales worked towards different targets: their activities were not synchronised.
So the answer is Lack of coordination; 15,000 fans 25 percent unsold.
